newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt pledges to keep CIC's identity.
newsitem.headline: French govt pledges to keep CIC's identity.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis pledged on Wednesday that the identity of the 11 regional banks which make up state-owned domestic banking group CIC would be preserved when it is privatised.
Conditions laid down for the sale of CIC, owned by state-controlled insurer GAN, "stipulate very clearly the preservation of the CIC network", he said.
"This rules out that the identity...of the big regional banks of the CIC group should be put into question when it is privatised," he told parliament in response to questions.

Last week, CIC chairman Bernard Yoncourt criticised bids made by two French banks believed to be the only serious bidders for CIC. He said the purchase by either Societe Generale or Banque Nationale de Paris could sound "the death knell" for CIC.
He expressed concern that the 11 regional banks would risk losing their strong individual identity and some might be closed down as part of a merger with either of their two rivals.
His fears are shared by the CIC banks, some of which have argued in favour of a form of mutualisation as an alternative.
Arthuis renewed an attack on Yoncourt for making the remarks midway through the sell-off process.

"You must understand this procedure has to be accompanied by a certain neutrality. It's not the place of the chairman of this group to express himself publicly, to put into doubt one or another candidate. It's not acceptable," he said. Last week, Arthuis hinted he might take reprisals against the chairman.
GAN, which reported on Wednesday that its first half loss swelled to 965 million francs from a loss of 387 million francs, is selling 67 percent of CIC as a prelude to its own privatistaion.
The government is examining offers for CIC but there are press reports that they are for substantially less than the 14.6 billion franc value placed on the bank in GAN's books.
GAN chairman Jean-Jacques Bonnaud said on Wednesday that the insurer would expect to be compensated by the state for any loss it suffered on the sale of CIC.
CIC contributed 472 million francs to GAN's results compared with 387 million francs last time.
